abstract:
Can the forces and particles of the Standard Model be read off the structure of conformal spinors (twistors)? [[t]] For the smallest composite that can have mass, the symmetries that respect its structure are exactly those behind the strong, weak and hypercharge forces. [[c:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite]]

The trail follows that observation to the precise gauge group, the quarks and leptons with their hypercharges, and the weak angle, several steps holding only under Hypothesis (S). [[c:standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics]] With the derived content alone the weak angle runs to the wrong value; an intermediate Pati-Salam symmetry repairs the running. [[c:standard-model.chain]]

It then takes up the Higgs field, the series' rung field, recorded as an elementary field of two doublets. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]] The route that would generate the weak scale from quantum corrections alone makes definite predictions that differ from the Standard Model, and current data go against them on three independent counts. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]] The working branch takes the weak scale as an input. [[c:synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number]]
introduction:
The walk goes from symmetries to the group, then to the particle content and its charges, then to the running of the forces, and ends with the Higgs field and the weak scale. [[t]]

Two postulates are listed first. [[t]] One adopts the standard indefinite inner product for the gauge fields, which the running of the forces uses. [[c:synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields]] The other registers the constant that sets the weak scale as a free number of the laws. [[c:synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number]]

Results a step rests on but that are not on the trail are listed at the end. [[t]]
i:standard-model: These results derive the Standard Model's symmetries and one generation of its matter from composites of conformal spinors, test the running of the forces against experiment, and then confront the series' Higgs field with data. [[t]]
t:^>standard-model.internal-symmetry-lad:
We start from how conformal spinors describe particles: one is massless, and a massive particle needs at least two. [[c:mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula]]

The mixings of $n$ conformal spinors that preserve total momentum and total helicity form exactly $U(n)$, giving the ladder \[ U(1), \quad U(2), \quad U(3) \] [[c:standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder]]
t:standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladde:
A composite has two levels of internal structure: which conformal spinor, and which of its three internal pairs. [[c:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite]]

The automorphism algebra of the minimal massive hierarchy $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ is \[ \su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1), \] exactly the Standard Model's. [[c:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite]] Three spinors instead, $\C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$, give a seventeen-dimensional algebra, which is too large. [[c:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite]]
t:standard-model.global-form-quotient-de:
The restriction on charges is directly testable. [[t]]

The $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ charge lattice forbids any fractionally charged colour singlet, so finding one would refute this part of the framework. [[c:pred.z6-charge-lattice]] Searches so far have found none. [[c:pred.z6-charge-lattice]]
With the symmetries fixed, the next question is what matter the composite carries. [[t]] The pair-level cells carry the quark doublet $(2,3)_{1/6}$ unconditionally. [[c:standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content]]

Under Hypothesis (S), one slot with the pairs full gives the lepton doublet \[ (2,1)_{-1/2} \] and without that hypothesis no lepton appears. [[c:standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content]]
t:standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-leve:
Next come the charges that decide how these particles feel the electroweak force. [[t]]

Under Hypothesis (S) for the doublets, the composite's states carry the observed hypercharges of one generation. [[c:standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency]] They satisfy all four anomaly conditions and are the unique solution for that content with \[ Y_{Q} = \tfrac16 \] [[c:standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency]]
t:standard-model.hypercharge-global-form:
Under the same hypothesis the whole state space of the composite can be seen at once. [[t]] It is the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3})$, the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ spinor. [[c:standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor]]

Its even half is exactly one generation, \[ Q \oplus L \oplus u^{c} \oplus d^{c} \oplus e^{c} \oplus \nu^{c}, \] sixteen-dimensional and including a right-handed neutrino, while the odd half is the antiparticles. [[c:standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor]]
t:standard-model.under-s-composites-stat:
A full generation with its charges lets us compute the weak angle, which measures how the electromagnetic and weak forces share out between them. [[t]]

Over one derived generation, with the lepton under Hypothesis (S), \[ \frac{\sum T_{3}^{2}}{\sum Q^{2}} = \frac{3}{8} \] [[c:standard-model.weak-angle-over-derived-generation]] That is $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ at unification, under the hypothesis that the particles fit into one simple group. [[c:standard-model.weak-angle-over-derived-generation]]
t:standard-model.weak-angle-over-derived:
The value $3/8$ holds at the unification scale, so the next step runs it down to where it is measured. [[c:standard-model.weak-angle-over-derived-generation]]

At one loop with the record inputs, the derived content with one imported Higgs doublet predicts \[ \sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z}) = 78761/379488 \approx 0.2075 \] against the measured $0.2312$, refuting the desert. [[c:standard-model.spectrum-run]] The supersymmetric coefficients would give $0.2309$, so the framework's $3/8$ survives only if the running differs from that of the derived content. [[c:standard-model.spectrum-run]]
t:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-m:
Before pinning down the group, the argument can be run the other way, to ask what the forces say about spacetime. [[t]]

If the gauge algebra is the automorphism algebra of the minimal massive composite, and mass begins at two constituents, then the Standard Model algebra forces four dimensions among the even dimensions. [[c:standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse]] Run backwards, the observed forces require a two-by-three structure, and both directions rest on that reading of the forces, which is stated as a premise. [[c:standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse]]
t:standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-:
An algebra fixes the symmetries only near the identity, so the next step pins down the group itself. [[t]]

It is \[ S(U(2) \times U(3)) \cong \bigl(SU(2) \times SU(3) \times U(1)\bigr)/\mathbb{Z}_{6}, \] the smallest of the Standard Model's global forms. [[c:standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined]] That quotient restricts which combinations of colour, weak charge and hypercharge any particle can carry. [[c:standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined]]
t:standard-model.spectrum-run>standard-m:
The failed run leaves two ways out: partner-like particles, which the series does not derive, or an enlarged symmetry at an intermediate energy. [[c:standard-model.spectrum-run]]

Under Hypothesis (S) the series supplies the second, the Pati-Salam symmetry, and with it the three couplings meet at one loop, with the intermediate scale between about $10^{10}$ and $10^{12}$ GeV and unification near $10^{16}$ GeV. [[c:standard-model.chain]] Below the intermediate scale the chain uses one Higgs doublet. [[c:standard-model.chain]]
t:standard-model.chain>synthesis.one-loo:
The running so far used coefficients taken from the literature. [[t]]

They now come out of the series' own algebra, as spin traces in the spacetime algebra, with the numbers of generations and Higgs doublets left as inputs. [[c:synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces]] Three generations give $b = (\tfrac{41}{10}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, -7)$ with one doublet and $(\tfrac{21}{5}, -3, -7)$ with two. [[c:synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces]] The computation uses the indefinite inner product for the gauge fields, the first postulate. [[c:synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces]]
t:synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficient:
So the number of Higgs doublets matters, and the rest of the trail asks what the series says about its scalar sector. [[t]]

The series' Higgs candidate is the rung field, which lives in the extra directions that transport adds; transport fixes one combination of its two halves through the cosmological constant. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus]] On that locus the field's one neutral physical mode is the rung unit, a boost of the rung frame, so the Higgs boson is a ripple of that scale. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus]] Read with the Hermitian norm, the W and Z masses come out in the electroweak pattern. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus]]
t:synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus:
Next comes the simplest action for the rung field. [[t]]

It is a D-term potential whose hypercharge part carries one constant shift, the level $\xi$; it keeps electric charge unbroken and puts the vacuum at a frame fixed by the level. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus]] So the weak scale is an input, set by $\xi$, as the second postulate records. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus]]

The tree masses are rigid: the Higgs weighs exactly $M_{Z}$ and a charged pair exactly $M_{W}$, which the measured Higgs mass rules out, so a second term $W(N)$ in the potential is needed. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus]]
t:synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and:
Masses for the quarks need a reading of how the rung field couples to them. [[t]]

The reading the series adopts is the one covariant under the right-handed rotations, with one family matrix on the field and another on its conjugate, the flavour structure of a left-right bidoublet. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix]] Equal matrices would make up and down quarks equally heavy, so the top's mass must come from the conjugate's own coupling. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix]] In this reading the charged pair couples to quarks about as strongly as the quarks' own mass couplings. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix]]
t:synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-c:
Since the level is put in by hand, a natural question is whether the weak scale could instead arise from quantum corrections alone. [[t]]

This is the Gildener-Weinberg route: with a scale-free tree potential the Higgs mass comes entirely from one loop, \[ 8\pi^{2}v^{2}m_{h}^{2} = 6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4} + 2m_{\pm}^{4} - 12m_{t}^{4} - \ell \] [[c:synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev]]

The top quark makes the Standard Model's own sum negative, about $-(46\ \mathrm{GeV})^{2}$, and the rung field's charged pair restores it only if it weighs between $450$ and $456$ GeV. [[c:synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev]] The count assumes that the series' Majorana and Pati-Salam sectors decouple from the rung field, which on the present readings they do not, so the route is explored, not derived. [[c:synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev]]
t:synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-fi:
That count treated the rung field as confined to the null-lift locus. [[t]]

Quantised as an elementary field, with the spacetime volume element $I_{4}$ as its imaginary unit, the rung field is linear on all eight real components and carries a neutral normal pair besides the neutral mode and the charged pair. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]] In two-doublet language it is the scale-invariant two-doublet model, and the normal pair joins the scalon sum. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]]

Then the charged pair lies below $456$ GeV, the normal pair below $542$ GeV, and the Higgs decay to two photons stays below $0.900$ of the Standard Model rate for every allowed charged mass. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]] The Particle Data Group 2026 average, $1.10 \pm 0.06$, lies $3.3$ standard deviations above that bound. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]] So the transmutation branch makes a definite prediction that differs from the Standard Model, and current data go against it: the two-photon rate is one of three independent counts. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]] The earlier tree-level readings had already met data in the same way, the simplest potential putting the Higgs at exactly $M_{Z}$, which the measured Higgs mass rules out. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus]]
t:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neut:
The Standard Model manages with one doublet, so the count of two deserves a check. [[t]]

A one-doublet field meets the null-lift locus only in pure gauge, so two doublets follow from three readings taken exactly: the null-lift constraint, the Higgs as exactly the rung unit, and a linear field. [[c:synthesis.one-doublet-field-is-pure-gauge-on-the-null-lift-locus-so-two-doublets-need-the-exact-constraint]] At any finite constraint coupling one doublet reproduces the rung-unit direction to relative order $H^{2}/v^{2}$, about $10^{-88}$, so nothing measurable at present separates the two counts. [[c:synthesis.one-doublet-field-is-pure-gauge-on-the-null-lift-locus-so-two-doublets-need-the-exact-constraint]]
t:synthesis.one-doublet-field-is-pure-ga:
On the transmutation branch the two doublets meet a second strike. [[t]]

The scalon sum forces large quartic couplings, and run upward in the series' own variables some quartic reaches $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-strong-coupling-within-a-few-tev-on-the-transmutation-branch]] There the two-loop terms are already 30 to 70 percent of the one-loop ones, so the branch is a strongly coupled theory not far above the weak scale. [[c:synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-strong-coupling-within-a-few-tev-on-the-transmutation-branch]]
t:synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-s:
The third strike comes from flavour. [[t]]

Under the adopted coupling with symmetric family matrices, the neutral normal pair couples down quarks through the up-quark mass matrix, so it turns a bottom quark into a strange or down quark at tree level. [[c:synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch]] With both masses at most $542$ GeV it would make $B_{s}$ and $B_{d}$ mesons mix with their antiparticles more than $50$ times faster than measured, for every split of the two masses. [[c:synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch]] So, under that coupling, the transmutation branch is excluded. [[c:synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch]]
conclusion:
From the symmetries of the smallest massive composite the trail has recovered the Standard Model's forces and, under Hypothesis (S), a full generation of matter as half the states of the composite. [[c:standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor]] The derived content alone runs the weak angle to the wrong value, and the Pati-Salam chain repairs the running. [[c:standard-model.chain]]

In the scalar sector the series' Higgs field is the rung field, quantised as an elementary linear field of two doublets, a count that holds only when three readings are taken exactly. [[c:synthesis.one-doublet-field-is-pure-gauge-on-the-null-lift-locus-so-two-doublets-need-the-exact-constraint]] Generating the weak scale from quantum corrections alone, the transmutation branch, gives definite predictions that differ from the Standard Model. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]] Under the adopted coupling reading it is excluded three times over: by the two-photon rate, by $B$-meson mixing, and by quartic couplings that grow strong within a few TeV. [[c:synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum]]

The working branch is the one with a level, where the second doublet must lie at about $2.5$ TeV or above. [[c:synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch]] On it the level $\xi$ is an input, a second free number of the laws beside $N$, not derived. [[c:synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number]] How the chain's scales move with a second doublet between a few TeV and the intermediate scale is left open. [[c:standard-model.chain]]
